verdict.rationale: Pipecat's official CLI ran keylessly and non-interactively in a runtime probe, and it exposes `eval` (behavioral evals against the real agent) and `cloud` (deploy). A Cloud REST API with an OpenAPI spec also supports programmatic automation, so headless operation is real. No evidence documents CI usage itself, such as CI recipes, non-interactive flags, exit codes for eval pass/fail, or pipeline examples. missing for 10: documented CI/CD integration guide, explicit headless/non-interactive run mode docs, eval exit-code/CI reporting, independent reports of CI usage

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: the official Pipecat CLI (pypi pipecat-ai[cli]) ran keylessly via uvx — `pipecat --help` lists init (project scaffolding), cloud (deploy to Pipecat Cloud), eval (behavioral evals)

You describe a conversation and the behavior you expect, and Pipecat runs it against your real agent (the same pipeline, the same services, the same code) and tells you whether the expectation still holds.
The private API (/v1...) manages agents, secrets, builds, regions, and organization settings.
